Parties

Party planners across Australia

Birthdays, milestones, engagements and kids parties. A party planner works to shorter lead times than a wedding planner and usually arrives with the entertainment and hire relationships already in hand.

What does a party planner do?

A party planner takes a celebration that is not a wedding and turns it into something you can attend rather than run. That covers the theme and styling, the venue or the set-up at home, the catering, the cake, the entertainment, the hire items, the timings and the pack down.

The rhythm of the job is different from wedding planning. Parties are usually planned in six to sixteen weeks rather than a year, the budgets are smaller, and a much larger share of the work is supplier wrangling in a short window. A party planner earns their fee mostly by already knowing who is good, who is available at short notice, and who will actually turn up.

Party planning services are also more likely to be sold as a fixed package than wedding planning is, because the scope is more predictable. That makes party planner cost easier to compare between quotes, provided you check what the package excludes.

Kids parties

Kids birthday parties

A kids birthday party planner is solving a different problem from an adult party planner: the guests are small, the window is two hours, and the parents are watching.

Most Australian kids parties run to a tight shape. Two hours, an activity or entertainer in the middle, food that small children will actually eat, and a hard finish before somebody melts down. A kids birthday party planner builds that shape and books the pieces: the entertainer, the soft play or jumping castle, the cake, the styling and the party bags.

Venue is the first decision and it drives everything else. At home you control the timing and save on hire, but you also host, clean and manage the weather. A hall or a party venue costs more and removes most of the work. A park is the cheapest and needs the most planning, and in many Australian council areas a park booking or permit is required for larger groups or for anything with an inflatable, which is the detail people most often miss.

Where a party planner earns their fee here is in the schedule. A two hour kids party has about four moving parts, and the difference between a good one and a chaotic one is almost entirely the order they happen in.

Entertainment is a separate booking

Entertainers, face painters, jumping castles and soft play are usually booked as suppliers rather than provided by the planner. Ask whether your quote includes the booking or just the recommendation.

Check the park rules early

Council park bookings and permits for inflatables often need more notice than the party does. Ask about this in the first conversation, not the last.

Adults

Milestone birthdays and surprise parties

Milestone birthdays

Thirtieths, fortieths, fiftieths and beyond. These behave more like small weddings than like kids parties: a venue, a guest list of 60 to 120, catering, drinks, a run sheet and speeches. The usual lead time is three to four months.

Party planning services

Surprise parties

A surprise party planner is managing a second, hidden timeline: who knows, who does not, how the guest of honour arrives and what the cover story is. The planning is normal. The communication plan is the hard part, and it is the reason people hire help.

Engagement parties

The first party after the yes, usually 40 to 80 guests and planned in three to four months. Often the first time a couple works with a planner at all.

Engagement party planning

Private parties at home

Anniversaries, retirements, christenings and long lunches. Planning a party at home is mostly a logistics problem: parking, power, wet weather plan, where the caterer works and how the hire truck gets in.

Cost

What a party planner costs

Party planning is more often quoted as a flat package than as a percentage, which makes it easier to compare than wedding planning.

There is less published Australian benchmark data for party planner cost than there is for weddings. What the wedding figures tell you still applies to the shape of the pricing: Airtasker's Australian guide reports planners commonly charging 10 to 15 per cent of total budget or hourly rates of $70 to $120, and Australian agency FAME Events describes flat planning fees starting from around $5,000 for a straightforward event, with a percentage model of 15 to 20 per cent used less often.

For a party, the practical version is this. A small kids party with entertainment and styling is usually a fixed fee well below the figures above. A 100 guest milestone birthday with a venue, catering, drinks and a band sits much closer to full event planning territory. The three things that move it are guest count, how many suppliers need managing, and whether the venue is dry hire, because a dry hire venue means the planner is building the infrastructure as well as the party.

Choosing one

What to check before you book a party planner

Party planning has a lower barrier to entry than wedding planning, so the range of experience you will encounter is wider. Five checks separate a professional from an enthusiast.

Have they run your size of party?

A planner who is excellent at 25 guests in a backyard is not automatically the right choice for 120 in a hall, and the reverse is just as true. Ask for the closest comparable event they have run.

Do they carry public liability insurance?

Most venues and many councils require the supplier to hold it, and some will not allow bump in without a certificate of currency. Ask for it early rather than the week before.

Who is on site, and for how long?

For a party, the planner is often also the person running the day. Confirm the arrival time, the finish time and what happens if the party runs over.

What do they book, and what do you book?

Some party planners manage every supplier booking. Others recommend and leave the booking to you. Both are legitimate. Only one of them takes the admin off you.

What is the wet weather plan?

For anything outdoors or at home, ask what happens if it rains and by what time the call gets made. A planner without an answer has not run enough outdoor events.

Straight answers

Party planner questions

What does a party planner cost in Australia?

There is little published national benchmark data specifically for party planner cost. The Australian wedding figures give the shape: Airtasker reports hourly rates of $70 to $120 and a common 10 to 15 per cent of budget model, and FAME Events describes flat planning fees from around $5,000 for a straightforward event. A small kids party sits well below that. A 100 guest milestone birthday sits much closer to it.

How far ahead should I book a party planner?

Three to four months is the usual window for a milestone birthday or engagement party. Kids parties are commonly planned in six to ten weeks. The constraint is rarely the planner. It is the entertainer, the venue and the jumping castle, all of which book out on Saturdays in term time.

Can a party planner organise a party at my house?

Yes, and at-home parties are a large part of the work. The planning is mostly logistics: access for the hire truck, power for catering equipment, a wet weather plan, where staff work and how the pack down happens without the last guests watching it.

Do party planners book the entertainment?

Usually they book it on your behalf rather than provide it themselves. Entertainers, face painters, inflatables and soft play are separate suppliers. Ask whether your quote includes managing those bookings or only recommending them.

Can a party planner keep a surprise party secret?

Yes, and managing the secret is part of the brief. A surprise party planner runs a second communication plan alongside the normal one, covering who is told, what the cover story is and how the guest of honour arrives. Tell the planner it is a surprise in the first message, because it changes how they contact you.
